title: I'm going to drop it
author: Upbeat_Ad_6119
selftext:
I've been working on this game for the last 3 weeks, putting in 12+ hours a day. Throughout this time, I was extremely enthusiastic. I was planning to make a demo by the end of this month and publish it on Steam, but... today, I feel like I've lost all my motivation.

I love how this game looks, how it feels, and how it sounds. I've put so many interesting mechanics into it that I can't even fit them all into a single video. But I guess I'm not capable of pushing this game to the finish line.

The main problem is the concept. I didn't even have one initially; I only came up with it along the way. In theory, it sounds kinda interesting: *"A cozy action-adventure where you explore 8 different, unique realms, searching for energy shards to bring these places back to life."*

It's not a revolutionary idea, but I think it could work well if it were wrapped up properly. The problem is, I can't do that.

Creating 8 different realms, each with 4–5 unique creatures, a boss fight, and small quests, would take an enormous amount of time and effort. And realistically, the potential profit wouldn't justify that investment.

Overall, this has been an incredibly valuable experience. I've learned a lot, but now I feel like I should try something else. Maybe a different direction, maybe a different genre, or maybe game development just isn't for me.

I'm not looking for a motivational speech. I just wanted to share this with someone before closing this chapter of my life. But I'd also appreciate some honest feedback on what I've done so far and how well I've done it.

replies.author: GoGs0l0dev
replies.body:
Holy shit man.  This is absolutely NOT the hardest part.  V1 and V2 are both 1 out of 10.  Of all the things Astra and other new models struggle with, visuals is not one of them.  You can literally have it go watch a YouTube video of how ESPN 2K5 did face generation for rookies, give it a detailed description of how you want the character models (less realistic, photorealistic, painted, etc.)

And have it set up 75 portraits for light, medium, and dark skin tones.  Have it add an assortment of 3-5 things such as few neck/face tattoos, a nose ring, etc.  and have it create 10-15 hair cuts that can be superimposed over the character portrait.

Boom you basically have an assortment of 5,000+ different character portraits that look much much better.

Shitty character portraits is not the thing you should be struggling with using AI for game development.

replies.author: Upbeat_Ad_6119

Why does everyone insult me by saying that I haven't put in much effort? And why are you drawing conclusions based on just one case when you know nothing about my background?

I know that three weeks is nothing in game development, okay? I've been a software engineer for over eight years, mostly working on backend development. I just decided to give game development a try. If it works out, it works out.

I never said that you should give up on something just because it doesn't work out. I never said I had high expectations, and I'm not frustrated because I can't achieve certain results in a few weeks when other people have spent decades learning this stuff.

And yeah, I know what it's like to learn something new, struggle with it, and eventually overcome every obstacle along the way. I've been doing that every day for all these years.

Everyone has their own unique path, and we know what's best for ourselves. What I shared was that, for me, the better option might be to drop this particular game, or even game development altogether, and move on to something else. That's my own way, why should i be hated for that?

comments.author: AkiraVero
comments.body:
It looks good. From looking at it I think you took a very similar approach as I am taking with my game (in terms of visual style, anyway). You've done well for what you have, good work!

As far as your feelings and the conflict you have - I guess only you can really decide. I know where you are coming from because I have had the same exact feelings.

Why are you doing game development? As a hobby? Just for fun? Or are you looking at it from an "investment" point of view and potential future?

If you love how it looks, feels and sounds and you are enjoying developing it and getting valuable experience out of it, I wouldn't give up. Why stop? You've hit the "hard" part. The part where you have to put a lot more manual effort and thought and design process into your game. If you do want to continue doing game development in the future, this is what makes you or breaks you. That's what separates you from a vibe coder just feeding prompts into an AI and telling the AI "give me recommendations and then saying "go with your best recommendation""

Like you said, if you can't justify the time and "potential profit" and it's not fun for you, then I agree. Your looking at it from an investment perspective. Making a large-scale game profit wise is usually not worth it instead of having a core concept already figured out and making a game out of it and sticking to that core loop.

Feel free to ignore whatever I said, I know you said your not looking for a motivational speech or anything like that, but I feel like you wrote what you wrote for a reason and not just for someone to say "nice game". (which it is!).

comments.author: Fuzzzy420
comments.body:
Hi There,
Strangely people in this community only accepts stuff that it's very polished or very unique or just very good. So many people get hate here I even though about starting another community with stricter rules on how to behave. 
Rule 1: calling a game slop has to come with an explanation 
Rule 2: post whatever you want about your game as long as it is about the process and not marketing
Rule 3: no marketing your game. 
Role 4: be nice even to slop. 

The problem with your post is in your paragraph 3 and the critical error you did. Design will not equal fun. You can have a great game but mediocre or bad gameplay. Start the other way around. What makes a gameplay loop fun to you!! Not to anyone else but you! 
Is the loop fun with shitty graphics? Then you can start developing for real. 

I did the same mistake so many times the eventually I learned 😜
You used the 3 weeks to build things that look nice, now spend the next three weeks building a gameplay loop that's fun, without touching your codebase!!! Use the same tech stack and start fresh until they Gameplay Loop is awesome, then bring it together. 
If you start bringing in the loop into your project as it's, you will get distracted over and over and have huge content but no fun. 

Just my recommendations, that's how I would do it. Don't give up, you already did A lot. 


I don't get the hate either ,I think you shouldn't have posted the video. That made the post about the game and not the process. Or rather show the process and not the result. 

Best skill i use: /roastme

comments.author: Rob-Gardner
comments.body:
So even though this is aigamedev, there are a lot of anti ai people in here just waiting for the opportunity to take shots...  

The advantage to these tools is that they can do work when they arent actively at the computer..  So rather than think of this project in massive scope..  Break it into chunks..  Brainstorm one boss and one realm.. talk it through with your system, develop an architecture for it.  Clearly plan out the mechanics and visuals, and then let it cook.  While it cooks brainstorm #2... and so on..  

I think you\`ll be surprised how you progress if you just focus on a simple creative addition at a time.
